stem: A file is encrypted for the recipients, and a separate hash is published so they can detect a change. Which CIA legs are those?
choices: Confidentiality, then integrity
Availability, then confidentiality
Both availability
The hash encrypts the file, so encryption is unnecessary
explanation: Encryption keeps the wrong people from reading the file. A hash that no longer matches shows the file changed. Availability is whether the file is there when needed. A hash is not encryption.
choiceNotes: Encryption hides the contents. The hash shows they were not modified.
Availability is uptime. These tools are not both aimed at it.
Neither control is primarily about the file being online.
A hash is a one-way fingerprint. It does not hide the file.

stem: An emergency firewall change was never ticketed. The only person who knows the new rule is on vacation when it causes an outage. What failed?
choices: The emergency change was not documented or reviewed, so nobody else can own it
Emergency changes are forbidden even when the business is down
The failure is that an emergency was allowed to exist
Leaving the rule undocumented was the correct emergency process
explanation: Emergencies happen. The control is to record and review them afterward so the change can be kept or backed out by someone else. A rule that lives in one person's memory cannot be fixed on vacation. The existence of the emergency is not the failure.
choiceNotes: Write it down and review it. Ownership has to survive one person being out.
Change management includes an emergency path. It does not pretend outages wait for a monthly meeting.
The emergency itself is not the process failure. The missing record is.
An undocumented rule is why the next person could not fix the outage.

stem: Someone runs a public exploit against one small website, brags in a forum, and never builds custom malware or keeps long-term access. Which actor fits?
choices: An unskilled attacker
A nation-state team that stays quiet for months
An insider who already has a badge
An organized crew with a payment site and affiliates
explanation: A public tool, a public brag, and no persistence are the unskilled end of the scale. A nation-state hides and stays. An insider already belongs inside. Organized crime runs the attack like a business. None of those match a one-off public exploit.
choiceNotes: Public tools and no follow-through are the unskilled pattern.
A nation-state does not usually announce a noisy one-day hit on a tiny site.
An insider does not need a public exploit against the outside website.
A payment site and affiliates are a criminal business, not a forum brag.

stem: Four hospitals share one cloud built only for their members. Outsiders cannot buy a tenancy in it, and no single hospital owns the whole platform. Which deployment is that?
choices: Community
Public, open to any customer with a credit card
Private to one hospital and unused by the other three
A cold site with no systems installed
explanation: A community cloud is shared by organizations with a common need and is not sold to the general public. A public cloud takes any customer. A private cloud serves one organization. A cold site is empty recovery space, not a running platform for four members.
choiceNotes: Shared by a defined group, and closed to everyone else, is a community deployment.
A public cloud would let outsiders buy in. This one does not.
Private means one organization. Four members break that definition.
A cold site is not where their workloads run day to day.

stem: A build server refuses an unsigned hotfix. The developer wants the check disabled for speed. What is the control?
choices: Code signing. Sign the hotfix instead of skipping the check
Code signing proves there are no bugs
Skipping the check is safe when someone is in a hurry
The signature encrypts the binary
explanation: A signature shows the binary came from the release key and was not swapped. It does not prove the code is bug-free. The hotfix should be signed. Skipping the check is how a tampered binary lands. Signing is not confidentiality.
choiceNotes: Keep the check and sign the binary. The hurry is not a reason to accept an unsigned file.
A signature answers who produced it, not whether the logic is correct.
Disabling the signature check is the hole. Speed does not make an unsigned hotfix trustworthy.
A signature leaves the bytes readable and verifies them. It does not hide them.

stem: A vendor's questionnaire claims full-disk encryption, and the contract includes a right to audit. No evidence has been produced. What is weak about accepting the form alone?
choices: A questionnaire is a claim. The audit right exists so you can ask for evidence
Questionnaires are always false and should never be used
A right to audit means you must not look
Encryption cannot be evidenced
explanation: Questionnaires are a cheap starting point and they are self-reported. Evidence or the audit right checks a claim that matters. You do not skip the form, and you do not treat it as proof. The right to audit is the right to look.
choiceNotes: Ask for evidence on the claims that carry risk. The form is not the proof.
Questionnaires are useful. They are not the last step.
The audit clause is wasted if you refuse to use it.
A vendor can show how encryption is deployed.

stem: Developers keep shipping injection bugs, and reception keeps letting visitors follow them through the door. Everyone watched the same generic annual video. What training change fits?
choices: Role-based training: secure coding for developers and physical social engineering for reception
A longer copy of the same generic video
Removing the report button
A rule that forbids mentioning phishing or tailgating
explanation: People need the risks of their own job. Developers need secure coding. Reception needs tailgating and pretext. A longer generic video still never names either job. Removing the report path and banning the topic make the failures quieter.
choiceNotes: Match the lesson to the work. That is role-based awareness.
More of the same video still skips both jobs.
The report path is how those failures get to the security team.
Forbidding the topic does not teach either group.
